# CVE-2020-14343: Improper Input Validation in PyYAML

### Technical Details

| Package Name | Ecosystem | Vulnerable Versions | First Patched Version |
 ---  --- |
| PyYAML | pip | < 5.4 | 5.4 |

### WAF Protection Rules

#### WAF Rule [...] The vulnerability stemmed from FullLoader inheriting dangerous YAML constructors from FullConstructor. The commit a001f27 explicitly moved these three multi-constructors (python/module, python/object, python/object/new) from FullConstructor to UnsafeConstructor, indicating they were the incomplete fix from CVE-2020-1747. These functions allowed instantiation of arbitrary Python objects when processing untrusted input with `FullLoader.full_load`.

This CVE has already been fixed in RHEL-9 with initial release of PyYaml v5.4-1.

Ansible Tower 3.7 uses affected version of PyYAML 3.12 from RHEL, but the use of load() is specified with a SafeLoader when it is called. So Ansible Tower and Ansible Engine are not affected.

Red Hat Quay, from version 3.4 uses the safe\_load function which is not affected by this issue. See . [...] ## Description

A vulnerability was discovered in the PyYAML library, where it is susceptible to arbitrary code execution when it processes untrusted YAML files through the full\_load method or with the FullLoader loader. Applications that use the library to process untrusted input may be vulnerable to this flaw. This flaw allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the system by abusing the python/object/new constructor. This flaw is due to an incomplete fix for CVE-2020-1747.
